note: Near-reference. Structural fix, evidence-based completion, partial-failure path, honest report.
submission:
Fix belongs in the harness, not the prompt. Build the work-list from list_invoices up front and hold it in the harness. Each invoice gets a terminal state - done, failed, or skipped - and the harness only writes a state when it has observed the compare_amounts tool result for that invoice id. The loop stops when every item has a terminal state, or the iteration cap is hit. The model's text is never consulted for termination.

Genuine failure: an invoice that will not fetch is marked failed after 3 retries and the loop continues, otherwise the new condition just turns a premature stop into an infinite loop.

Report: write_report is called by the harness from the state table, so the header reads '8 of 12 reconciled, 4 failed'. The report cannot claim more coverage than the table records.

note: Pure prompt-level fix. The exact instruction being proposed was already in the system prompt when the agent stopped at step 19.
submission: The system prompt needs to be much more explicit. I would add: 'You MUST process every single invoice in the list. Do not stop until all 12 invoices have been checked. Do not summarise early. Count the invoices you have processed before you finish.' I would also add an example showing the agent working through all items one by one, and remind it again at the end of the prompt.

note: Correct structural fix that creates an infinite loop on a genuinely unfetchable invoice. The most instructive near-miss in the set.
submission: Keep the list of invoice ids in the harness. After every model turn, check which ids have a recorded compare_amounts result. Loop until that set equals the full set of ids from list_invoices. Do not break the loop on the model saying it is finished - that claim is not evidence. The report is written only after the check passes.

note: Attributes the failure to model laziness and never names the missing harness invariant.
submission: Honestly this is just the model being lazy. It got bored after 4 invoices and decided that was enough, which is a known problem with these models on long repetitive tasks. I would switch to a stronger model and lower the temperature so it stays on task, and tell it that skipping work is unacceptable.

submission:
Fix harness mein hoga, prompt mein nahi. list_invoices se work-list banao aur harness mein rakho. Har invoice ka ek terminal state ho - done, failed ya skipped - aur state tabhi likho jab uss invoice id ka compare_amounts result actually mila ho. Model ka 'complete' bolna evidence nahi hai, use termination ke liye mat use karo.

Agar koi invoice sach mein fetch nahi ho rahi to retry ke baad usko failed mark karke aage badho, warna loop kabhi khatam hi nahi hoga.

Report harness state table se banegi, isliye woh '8 of 12 reconciled, 4 failed' likhegi - 12 of 12 nahi.

note: Proposes a cap, which bounds runaway loops but does nothing about a stop that came early. Structural, but not the right structure.
submission: Add a minimum and maximum iteration count to the harness. The agent cannot end the run before 12 iterations since there are 12 invoices, and it is force-stopped at 40. That way it cannot finish in 23 steps having only done 4 invoices, because the loop simply will not exit that early.

note: Fixes the damage (the false report) but not the cause (the loop). Tests that a4 and a2 are judged independently.
submission: The real harm was the report going to the client claiming everything was processed. The harness should build the report itself from the tool results it observed, not let the model compose it freely. Any invoice with no compare_amounts result is listed as not checked, so the finance team sees '4 checked, 8 not checked' and catches this before it leaves the building.

note: Everything except the report. Passing grade with one clean miss.
submission: Move the stopping condition out of the conversation. The harness owns a state table keyed by invoice id, populated only from observed compare_amounts results, and the loop runs until every row is terminal or the cap is reached. Terminal includes failed(reason) and skipped(reason), not just done - a single unfetchable invoice must not be able to hang the run forever, which is what you get if the only terminal state is success.

note: Gestures at verification without naming what evidence is collected or how the loop terminates.
submission: I would add a verification step at the end. After the agent thinks it is done, a second pass checks the work and if anything is missing it sends the agent back to finish. This way nothing gets missed and the report is accurate because it has been verified before it goes out.
